properties.title: Brain-JEPA: Brain Dynamics Foundation Model with Gradient Positioning and Spatiotemporal Masking
properties.contribution: Self-supervised fMRI representation learning with downstream prediction, classification, and prognostic endpoint evaluation.
properties.membership_rationale: A learned masked-target predictor is implemented, but a persistent health-world state advanced by that predictor is not established. This is unresolved core identity, not evidence that the method has no predictive representation value.

properties.interpretation_boundary: Downstream endpoint prediction is distinguished from evaluation of an evolving brain-state transition.

properties.name: Brain-JEPA
properties.configuration: Main ViT-B configuration pretrained for 300 epochs.
properties.artifact_resolution: Paper-documented configuration, not a uniquely verified checkpoint or one set of final weights across all tasks.
properties.predictor: Narrower ViT; depth 6, embedding dimension 384 for ViT-B
properties.input: Resting-state fMRI BOLD time series; 450 ROIs × 160 timesteps

properties.configuration_boundary: Size variants, framework ablations, task-specific fine-tuned models, and repeated runs are not one identical parameter artifact.

flow: Parcellate, robust-scale, and temporally downsample fMRI
Patchify, shuffle ROI order, and construct observation/target blocks

Evaluate separate fine-tuned or linear-probe readouts

evidence_fragments.content:
38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024).
arXiv:2409.19407v1  [q-bio.NC]  28 Sep 2024

With a Vision Transformer (ViT) as the observation encoderfθ, Brain-JEPA
employs a single observation block to predict the representations of target blocks.

Given the outputsx from the observation encoderfθ, the predictorgϕ is trained to predict
the three kinds of targetssry conditioned on the positional embeddingP (Figure 1). The training lossL
is the averageL2 distance between sry and its corresponding prediction:

It includes resting-state fMRI recordings with medical records from 40,162 participants
aged 44 to 83. Multi-site recordings were acquired with the temporal resolution of 0.735s. We allocated
80% of this dataset for pretraining (of which we calculated the group-level gradients as well), with the
20% held-out for downstream evaluation (internal tasks of age and sex prediction).

We used three datasets for external evaluation: HCP-Aging, as a segment of the public Human
Connectome Project (HCP) [45], includes resting-state fMRI from 656 healthy elderly participants.
It was used to predict traits (Neuroticism and Flanker score) and demographics (age and sex). The
Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) [ 46] was used for the early diagnosis and
prognosis of neurodegenerative diseases, with fMRI from 189 participants for normal control (NC)v.s.
mild cognitive impairment (MCI) classification, and 100 cognitively normal participants for amyloid
positive v.s. negative classification. Moreover, to assess generalizability across different ethnic groups
and real-world clinical applications, we included resting-state fMRI of Asian participants recruited by
Memory, Ageing and Cognition Centre (MACC), with 539 participants for NC v.s. MCI classification.

All fMRI data was parcellated into n = 450ROIs, using Schaefer-400 [47] for cortical regions and
Tian-Scale III [48] for subcortical regions. Robust scaling was implemented by subtracting the median
and dividing by the interquartile range, calculated across participants for each ROI [14]. Our default
input size is 160 timesteps for each of the 450 ROIs (i.e., 450×160). UKB and HCP-Aging used multi-
band acquisition with a high temporal resolution (TR≈ 0.7 seconds), while ADNI and MACC used
single-band acquisition with a lower resolution (TR≈ 2 seconds). To ensure consistency across datasets,
we standardized the temporal resolution by downsampling the multi-band data using a temporal stride
of 3, aligning the TR of all datasets to approximately 2 seconds. During the fine-tuning and linear
probing stage, all the downstream datasets were divided into a 6:2:2 ratio for training, validation, and
testing.

Brain-JEPA is pretrained without a [cls] token. For evaluation, we used the target encoder and average
pooled its output to generate a global fMRI representation. The main results in Section 4.3, along with
the analysis in Section 4.5, 4.6 and 4.7 were all based on ViT-B pre-trained for 300 epochs.

For the Asian disease cohort, all participants completed a locally validated neuropsychological test
battery, which assessed seven domains: executive function, attention, language, visuomotor speed,
verbal memory, and visual memory.

using
a threshold of global [18F]-Florbetapir amyloid PET SUVR >= 1.11 to define amyloid positivity [56].

Brain-JEPA sets
a potential foundation for integrating multimodal brain activity data such as MEG and EEG or even
brain structure data like T1-weighted MRI.

Ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of patient data while using such advanced AI systems is
paramount. While Brain-JEPA has shown superior performance across different tasks, continuous
monitoring for potential biases is essential, especially as the model is scaled and deployed in varied
clinical settings.

All main results in Table 1, 2, and 3 contain mean and standard deviation from
5 independent runs.

The
model checkpoints and anonymized code are provided in supplementary material with clear
instructions in the readme file.

The original papers that produced the code package or dataset are all properly
cited.

The datasets of human subjects used in this paper are either publicly available or
from previous work which will be cited upon acceptance.

For each
ROI, we first average the self-attention across its 10 patches. Next, we average the values of the ROIs
within each sub-network and normalize them to obtain the network-level attention distribution.

The parameter t represents the diffusion time, which controls the scale of the diffusion
process.

Instead of reconstructing masked inputs during
pretraining, Brain-JEPA predicts abstract representations of sampled targets from the observation.

This division forces the model to engage in forecasting time series,
generalizing across unseen ROIs, and predicting time series for unseen ROIs.

capability_assessments.rationale: Representation evaluation is established, but the ontology's strict identity guard for L0 requires an implemented persistent state and learned health-world transition. Those necessary conditions remain unresolved. Therefore neither a demonstrated L0 edge nor an L1–L4 label is assigned. This is not a negative judgment on representation quality or a definitive not_world_model classification. The legacy L0 cell is preserved as historical extraction.

gate_assessments.rationale: Provenance and leakage controls are partial. Training-only scaling fits, partition/overlap mechanics, and appropriate evidence-retention checks remain insufficiently documented. No leakage failure is asserted.
BP_COMPONENT does not require a validated temporal simulator. This exclusion is confined to the selected representation use; core identity and any upgrade to a forecast profile remain unresolved.
No multi-time state forecast is the evaluated product. Input context and epochs are not rollout horizons.
No probabilistic forecast guarantee or uncertainty-dependent decision is claimed for the selected use. Endpoint calibration remains unreported, not validated.
The documented component has no settable healthcare action input.
No intervention-effect interpretation is attached to the evaluated outputs. Functional gradients/attention are not identification.
No model-coupled optimizer or decision policy is implemented.
The scoped evaluation is offline representation research, not actual action-affecting clinical workflow. This does not waive privacy, ethics, prediction-risk, or future deployment safeguards.

External-cohort transfer with adaptation is evaluated, but overlap controls, exact split units, and scanner/site/population disentanglement are incomplete. E11's existence does not alone pass the stronger gate.
No human-output usability study or sim-to-real utility claim is the assessed product. Human imaging data are not a reader study.
No realized live-workflow/patient benefit is claimed as a completed experiment. Broader-impact benefits are prospective aspirations, not clinical utility evidence.
No defined operational release is established. Research code/checkpoint statements do not establish authorization, monitoring, or change control.

limitations: Automated model review, not independent human verification or replication.
This synthesis read all 26 supplied text pages and all supplied automated page-review notes. Earlier API page calls received images; this synthesis did not directly inspect images.
The source hash, page-call receipts, and file availability are supplied provenance, not independently recomputed or verified here.
No filesystem writes, repository inspection, supplementary checkpoint/code inspection, external citation verification, schema-validator execution, graph assembly, or regression tests were performed.

All 128 catalogue features have explicit dispositions, including unresolved and inapplicable states; this does not make every feature implemented, every source fact verified, or the package graph-admitted.
Core world-model identity remains unresolved. The prior unsupported L0 demonstration is removed rather than inventing persistent state/transition evidence to satisfy preflight.
The reported main configuration is not a unique checkpoint. Separate fine-tuned tasks, size variants, and training runs must not be treated as identical weights.
R2 uses stated held-out actual human fMRI evaluation. R3 remains partial under the stronger overlap-control requirement; external adaptation is not itself a disqualification.
Training-only group-gradient fitting is explicit. Training-only robust-scaling estimation, repeat-scan/family/site grouping, exact test counts, and participant overlap controls are incomplete.
AD conversion is a prognostic endpoint, but follow-up, sample size, and scan-to-outcome timing are not reported. It is not promoted to a world-state transition.
TRs, stride, input length, patch length, and epochs remain as reported. No derived durations, split counts, effective batch size, graphical endpoints, or clinical thresholds are added.
Main Tables 1–3 have mean/SD over five runs according to page 22. That definition is not automatically extended to additional tables.
MSE physical units/normalization, F1 conventions, statistical test details, multiplicity, and sources of run variability are insufficiently specified.
The general state-of-the-art claim has exceptions: BNT has higher main-table ADNI NC/MCI accuracy; BrainLM has lower HCP Flanker MSE.
Alpha/beta region labels, Table 2 text/image disagreement, Figure 6 prose/curve inconsistency, and mathematical notation questions remain queued.
Attention and functional coordinates do not establish causal biology, explanation fidelity, or clinical utility.
The Asian diagnostic battery says seven domains while enumerating six, and its supporting prior-work citation is deferred.
The authors identify limited compute, untested ViT-H, insufficient pretraining diversity, finer interpretation, and multimodal integration as limitations/future work.
Reported code/checkpoint availability is claim-stage only; actual assets, licenses, reproducibility, and release safety were not checked.
Checklist ethics conformity and NA declarations do not establish formal approval, exemption, consent, regulatory authorization, or true risk inapplicability.
No R4–R8 facet is established. Human scans are not human output review; offline outcomes and prospective aspirations are not prospective system use or patient benefit.
